A monk begins climbing a mountain path at exactly 7:00 AM and reaches the summit at exactly 7:00 PM, walking at varying speeds and resting at times along the way. The next day he starts back down the very same path at exactly 7:00 AM and reaches the bottom at exactly 7:00 PM, again varying his pace. Must there be some point on the path where he is located at exactly the same time of day on both days?
choices: No — it depends entirely on how fast he walks each day
Yes — this is guaranteed no matter how his pace varies each day
Only if the mountain path happens to be perfectly straight
No — only if he walks at a perfectly constant speed on both days

questions.q: Of three prisoners A, B, and C, the governor will pardon exactly one, chosen uniformly at random, though the result won't be announced until tomorrow. Prisoner A asks the guard, who already knows the outcome, to name one of B or C who will definitely NOT be pardoned — at least one such prisoner always exists no matter who is actually chosen. The guard truthfully says, 'C will not be pardoned.' Does this change A's own probability of being pardoned?
A woman says: 'The day before yesterday I was 25, and next year I will turn 28.' This is only true for one specific relationship between 'today' and her birthday. What must be true?
choices: No date makes this statement true
Today is December 31st and her birthday is January 1st
Today is January 1st and her birthday is December 31st

questions.q: A father and his son are in a car accident. The father dies at the scene, and the son is rushed to the hospital in critical condition. The surgeon looks at the boy and says, 'I can't operate on him — he's my son.' How is this possible?
choices: The surgeon is the boy's mother.
The boy has two adoptive fathers.
This is a logical contradiction with no answer.
The father secretly survived and is the surgeon.

questions.q: Rule: 'If a card has a vowel on one side, it has an even number on the other side.' You see four cards showing E, K, 4, 7. Which cards must you turn over to test the rule?

An ant starts crawling from one end of a 1 km rubber band at a constant 1 cm/s. At the end of every second, the entire band is instantly and uniformly stretched by another 1 km. Does the ant ever reach the far end?
choices: It depends on exactly where on the band the ant starts
Yes — the ant's fractional progress each second forms a divergent harmonic series, so it eventually covers the whole band
No — the band stretches far faster than the ant can crawl, so it falls further behind every second
No — the ant can only reach the end once the stretching stops
